masterBody:
Atlas shipped major billing hardening (CQRS refactor, per-tenant rate limiting, v1 endpoint removal) and closed a webhook HMAC timing vulnerability, while Lumen shipped Auth Tokens v2 (firm June 15 v1 sunset) plus large frontend quality upgrades (React 18.3, accessibility fixes, and a data-grid perf win). Forge shipped tab-bar navigation into TestFlight and stabilized iOS via crash + memory-leak fixes. The week’s top risks are (1) premium-tier launch gating blocked on DevOps LaunchDarkly configuration with no committed date, and (2) an exec-driven navigation reversal (tab bar → gesture nav) without a formal decision record, now blocking Forge deep-link routing and creating an active cross-squad UX conflict with Lumen’s user-testing-backed tab-bar preference.

## Highlights

- **[Atlas] Billing API** — ATLS-42 completed CQRS refactor splitting BillingService into query/command pattern; load tested at 5× peak. (ATLS-42)
- **[Atlas] Auth migration** — ATLS-55 migrated all token calls to Lumen’s `/api/auth/tokens/v2`, removing v1 dependencies ahead of the June 15 sunset. (ATLS-55)
- **[Atlas] Reliability** — ATLS-38 deployed per-tenant rate limiting (1000 req/min) with proper 429s; ATLS-29 removed `/billing/v1` endpoints with zero callers verified. (ATLS-38, ATLS-29)
- **[Atlas] Security** — GitHub PR #54 fixed webhook HMAC timing vulnerability using a monotonic clock approach. (PR #54)
- **[Lumen] Auth tokens v2 shipped** — GitHub #31 / Jira LMNE-22 released `/api/auth/tokens/v2` with `tenantId` + `scopes`; v1 deprecated with June 15 sunset; Atlas migration confirmed. (#31, LMNE-22)
- **[Lumen] Design tokens** — GitHub #34 / Jira LMNE-21 migrated component library to Figma-synced design tokens (dark + light). (#34, LMNE-21)
- **[Lumen] Performance** — GitHub #35 / Jira LMNE-20 reduced P99 scroll jank from 180ms to 22ms via stabilized row identity. (#35, LMNE-20)
- **[Lumen] Platform + quality** — GitHub #37 / Jira LMNE-19 upgraded React to 18.3; GitHub #38 / Jira LMNE-17 resolved 9 axe accessibility violations on form inputs. (#37, LMNE-19, #38, LMNE-17)
- **[Forge] Navigation** — FORGE-30 implemented tab bar (Home/Tasks/Notifications/Profile) with deep linking support; shipped to TestFlight. (FORGE-30)
- **[Forge] iOS stability** — FORGE-29 fixed a 12MB camera memory leak; FORGE-28 resolved an iOS 16 rotation crash with a regression test. (FORGE-29, FORGE-28)
- **[Forge] Widget + UX** — FORGE-31 shipped an iOS widget to TestFlight; FORGE-33 added haptic feedback on card swipes. (FORGE-31, FORGE-33)

## Risks & Blockers

- **[BLOCK]** **[Atlas]** ATLS-56 premium-tier feature flags are code-complete but blocked on LaunchDarkly configuration from DevOps with no confirmed delivery date.
- **[BLOCK]** **[Forge]** Navigation architecture conflict: an exec UX review reversed the sprint-planned (and TestFlight-shipped) tab bar direction toward gesture navigation without a formal decision record; this blocks downstream work.
- **[BLOCK]** **[Forge]** FORGE-36 deep-link routing cannot proceed until navigation architecture is finalized.
- **[BLOCK]** **[Lumen]** LMNE-24 is blocked on design-token migration completion: skeleton loader shimmer duration mismatch (1.5s in code vs 1.2s Figma spec) must be corrected before merge.
- **[HIGH]** **[Lumen]** LMNE-25: intermittent auth service 503s in CI (shared staging flakiness) have persisted for weeks and are blocking e2e tests; process gap noted (no formal Jira ticket despite repeated impact).
- **[WATCH]** **[Atlas]** ATLS-44 renewal test coverage is ~70%, targeting 85%.
- **[WATCH]** **[Lumen ↔ Forge]** Gesture navigation tension: Lumen is reverting gesture nav after user testing showed 67% tab-bar preference, while Forge design is pushing gesture nav—risk of inconsistent UX + duplicated work.
- **[WATCH]** **[Lumen]** Dark-mode token correctness flagged in prior accessibility audit may still be wrong; verification needed before token migration lands.

## Cross-Squad Dependencies

- **[Lumen → Atlas]** Auth tokens v2 shipped Monday (LMNE-22 / GitHub #31) → Atlas migrated in-week (ATLS-55), de-risking the firm June 15 v1 sunset.
- **[Forge ↔ Lumen]** Navigation pattern alignment required: Lumen’s user-testing-backed tab bar preference vs Forge’s gesture-nav direction risks inconsistent mobile UX and rework.
- **[Atlas ← DevOps]** Premium-tier launch is blocked on DevOps LaunchDarkly configuration for feature flags (ATLS-56).

## Roadmap Movement

- **[Atlas — Premium tier gating]** **At Risk** — implementation appears code-ready, but launch readiness is blocked on DevOps LaunchDarkly configuration (ATLS-56).
- **[Lumen — Auth modernization]** **On Track** — `/api/auth/tokens/v2` shipped (LMNE-22 / GitHub #31) and Atlas migrated (ATLS-55) ahead of the June 15 v1 sunset.
- **[Lumen — Design token system]** **At Risk** — large migration landed (LMNE-21 / GitHub #34), but blocked by shimmer spec mismatch (LMNE-24) and pending dark-mode token verification.
- **[Forge — Mobile navigation]** **Stalled** — direction reversal (tab bar → gesture nav) without a formal decision record blocks deep-link routing (FORGE-36) and downstream UX decisions.

## Open Discrepancies

- **[DECISION RECORD GAP] [Forge]** Navigation architecture reversed via exec UX review / Figma commentary rather than a formal engineering-backed decision record, despite tab bar already shipping to TestFlight.
  Evidence A: Tab bar implementation shipped (FORGE-30).
  Evidence B: Exec-driven gesture-nav pivot conflicts with shipped direction (FORGE-38 / Forge Figma).
  Conflict-resolution ruling: **Figma wins** for the most recent design decision, but this must be formalized with an explicit decision record and engineering sign-off before further implementation.
- **[PROCESS GAP] [Lumen]** CI/e2e testing blocked by intermittent auth service 503s for weeks without formal tracking.
  Evidence A: Shared staging flakiness blocking e2e tests (LMNE-25).
  Conflict-resolution ruling: **Slack is signal only**; open a Jira ticket and treat Jira as the system of record for status.
- **[DESIGN PATTERN CONFLICT] [Lumen ↔ Forge]** Gesture navigation vs tab bar: Lumen user testing shows 67% preference for tab bar and is reverting gesture nav (LMNE-26), while Forge design direction is pushing gesture nav.
  Evidence A: Lumen revert decision after user testing (LMNE-26).
  Evidence B: Forge navigation pivot direction (Forge Figma / FORGE-38).
  Conflict-resolution ruling: **Figma wins** for the latest design decision, but the cross-squad pattern must be resolved explicitly to prevent divergent implementations.

Conflict-Resolution Policy (Editable — see SE for changes)

- **Status of work (done vs in-progress)**: **Jira wins** — it is the PM system of record
- **What the code actually does**: **GitHub wins** — code is authoritative over descriptions
- **Design decisions**: **Figma wins** — latest dated version wins
- **Slack-only claims**: **Flag only** — never treat as authoritative; surface in Open Discrepancies

verdicts.claim: #56 updates billing API documentation with REST API reference and examples for all billing endpoints following the v2 refactor.
verdicts.reason: The source document directly confirms that PR #56 updates billing documentation with request/response examples for all billing endpoints following the v2 API refactor, matching all key elements of the claim.

verdicts.claim: ATLS-38: Rate limiting middleware deployed to billing API endpoints, enforcing 1000 req/min per tenant with 429 Retry-After responses
verdicts.reason: The source confirms the rate limiting specification (1000 req/min per tenant, 429 with Retry-After header) and that this is for billing API endpoints, but only states the ticket is "Done" without explicitly confirming that the middleware was actually deployed to production.

verdicts.claim: Found it — it was the EU replica lagging behind after the v1 endpoint removal migration.
verdicts.reason: The source document contains a direct quote from alex-kumar stating exactly this claim in the second message from that author.

verdicts.claim: Premium tier upgrade flow finalized with social proof section (customer logos) per growth team request, including three variants with 'B' variant prioritized for A/B testing.
verdicts.reason: The source document explicitly confirms that the upgrade modal includes a social proof section with customer logos per growth team request, specifies three variants exist in the file, and indicates the 'B' variant should be implemented first for A/B testing.

verdicts.claim: #32 fixes theme flickering on dark mode toggle by moving theme context initialization to synchronous effect before first paint.
verdicts.reason: The source document explicitly states in both the PR body and title that PR #32 "Resolves flash of wrong theme on toggle by moving theme context initialization to a synchronous effect before first paint," which directly matches the claim being verified.

verdicts.claim: LMNE-29: Data grid virtualization fix already being leveraged for sortable/filterable table view implementation
verdicts.reason: The source confirms LMNE-29 involves a sortable/filterable table view that reuses a data grid from LMNE-20, but does not explicitly mention "virtualization" or characterize LMNE-20 as a "virtualization fix."

verdicts.claim: The auth service in CI uses a shared staging environment — it's been flaky for weeks.
verdicts.reason: The claim is directly quoted verbatim from priya-nair's message in the source document, which explicitly states "The auth service in CI uses a shared staging environment — it's been flaky for weeks."

verdicts.claim: LMNE-21: Component library migration to design tokens completed with 300+ file changes and zero hardcoded hex values.
verdicts.reason: The source confirms the task completion (status: "Done"), zero hardcoded hex values requirement, and general migration scope, but does not mention the specific "300+ file changes" metric, so that quantitative detail cannot be verified.

verdicts.claim: #19 implements the iOS home screen widget small variant showing today's task count and next due item via WidgetKit shared App Group container.
verdicts.reason: The source document explicitly confirms all elements of the claim: PR #19 implements a WidgetKit small variant showing today's task count and next due item that reads from a shared App Group container.
The source document directly quotes mei-tanaka stating "Sprint 9 wrap: FORGE-28 ✅, FORGE-29 ✅, FORGE-30 ✅, FORGE-31 ✅, FORGE-33 ✅" which exactly matches the claim being verified.

verdicts.claim: A design experiment shouldn't reverse an engineering decision this late.
verdicts.reason: The source document contains a direct quote from carlos-mendez stating exactly this claim: "A design experiment shouldn't reverse an engineering decision this late."

verdicts.claim: FORGE-36: Deep link routing blocked on FORGE-30 tab bar completion and navigation architecture uncertainty.
verdicts.reason: The source document shows FORGE-36 is "In Progress" with no mention of blocking dependencies on FORGE-30 or navigation architecture uncertainty—it only documents the acceptance criteria for implementing deep link routing.

missingFacts: Tension 1 (Atlas ATLS-42 Jira/GitHub status mismatch): AI report does not surface the specific cross-source inconsistency that PR #51 was merged on May 22 but the Jira ticket remains "In Progress" — a data quality issue flagged as requiring VP attention.

Tension 3 (Lumen auth service incident root cause and process failure): AI mentions "intermittent auth service 503s" and a "process gap," but omits the critical detail that this was an OOM incident (not just flakiness), that it lasted 24+ hours, and that it was diagnosed and resolved entirely in Slack with an explicit request for a Jira ticket that was ignored — creating a significant operational/process red flag.

Tension 4 (design token migration blocking LMNE-24): AI mentions a "skeleton loader shimmer duration mismatch" blocking LMNE-24, but the ground truth does not contain this detail — this appears to be fabricated or sourced from outside the ground truth document.

Tension 5 (positive coordination story): AI report does not highlight the positive cross-team coordination exemplified by Atlas migrating to Lumen's Auth Tokens v2 in the same week it shipped — a key "should surface" item per scoring guidance.
Sprint completion rates: Not surfaced (velocity numbers, ticket closure counts per squad).
Lumen velocity: No mention of the 6 tickets closed in Sprint 12.
EU billing latency incident (ATLS-58): Not mentioned; this was a post-deployment outage that required same-day diagnosis and resolution.
Recommended actions/follow-ups: AI does not surface the three explicit action items (Forge design/EM sync within 48 hours; Lumen incident ticketing norm; ATLS-42 status update).
Legacy /billing/v1 deprecation cycle details (ATLS-29): Mentioned generically but missing the clean data-driven verification (zero callers via Datadog trace analysis) that demonstrates quality rigor.
